title: Congress leader sits in over missing CCTV at Patna vote counting centre
seoTitle: Patna sit-in over missing counting CCTV

tea.why: A Congress leader is staging a sit-in protest over the alleged absence of CCTV cameras inside the vote counting hall.
tea.want: Protesters want CCTV cameras installed inside the counting hall for the Legislative Council elections.
tea.changed: Oct 27: Congress leader Sanjay Yadav launched a sit-in protest at the Bankipur counting centre in Patna.

summary: On October 27, 2026, a Congress candidate staged a sit-in protest at the vote counting centre located at Bankipur Girls' School in Patna, Bihar. The demonstration began as counting commenced for the Bihar Legislative Council elections covering Graduates' and Teachers' constituencies. The protester raised concerns that CCTV surveillance cameras were missing from the actual hall where votes were being counted, warning that the lack of cameras raised suspicions of possible vote manipulation. Other opposition candidates also expressed surprise over the arrangements, while a Janata Dal (United) candidate dismissed the allegations, stating that the Election Commission of India closely monitors the process.
demands: Install CCTV cameras inside the vote counting hall
response: JD(U) candidate Neeraj Kumar downplayed the objections, questioning why opposition candidates raised allegations as soon as counting began. Magistrate Anugya stated that security checks were in place and entry was restricted to authorized pass-holders without mobile phones.

updates.text: A Congress leader launched a sit-in protest at the Patna counting centre alleging a lack of CCTV cameras in the counting area.
